subject: physics
question_text: What is meant by hydrostatic paradox?

mark_split.label: P = P₀ + ρgh, no shape term

verification.note: Asked in TS Inter I-Year Physics Paper-I, March 2019 (Q6) — Section A, 2 marks. The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: for a liquid at rest the pressure at a depth h below the free surface is P = P₀ + ρgh, which contains only the vertical height h, the density ρ and g. Vessels of different shape filled with the same liquid to the same height therefore have the same base pressure, however different the volumes of liquid they hold. With equal base areas the force on the base is equal too.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.margin_note: First mark. State the comparison: different shapes, same liquid height, same base pressure.
steps.why: The name paradox points at the surprise, so the statement has to carry the comparison. Without the different shapes at equal height there is nothing surprising to name.
common_mistakes: Saying the pressure at the base is the same even when the liquid heights differ. The heights must be equal.
Answering with the formula alone and never describing the vessels.

recall.must_convey: That vessels of different shapes filled to the same height with the same liquid have the same pressure at the base.
accept: same liquid to the same height
the amount of liquid does not matter
reject: P is P naught plus rho g h

steps.memory_tip: Different shapes, same liquid height, same base pressure. That is the paradox.

steps.label: P = P₀ + ρgh, no shape term

surface of a liquid at rest is
where P₀ is the atmospheric pressure, ρ is
the density of the liquid, g is the
acceleration due to gravity and h is the

Shape, volume and mass do not appear.

lines.text: P depends on h, ρ and g only

steps.margin_note: Second mark. The formula has no shape term, and saying so is what earns it.
steps.why: The formula is the explanation. Once a student sees that only h, ρ and g are in it, the equal base pressures stop being surprising.
common_mistakes: Taking h along the slant of a sloping vessel. Only the vertical height counts.
Saying the force on the base is also equal in every case. It is equal only when the base areas are equal.

recall.must_convey: That P = P naught plus rho g h, so the pressure depends only on the vertical height, the density and g.
accept: P naught plus rho g h
shape does not enter the formula

steps.memory_tip: Only h, ρ and g sit in P = P₀ + ρgh. No shape, no volume, no mass.

insider_note: One mark states the paradox, one gives P = P₀ + ρgh. The formula alone, with no vessels of different shape, reads as an unrelated answer.
